text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PD-1234 triggered for service 'redwood-runtime-latency' - 3 pages in 2m
sam: acked PD-1234 :white_check_mark:
maria: seeing brief latency bump on dedicated-pool-3, p50 ~ 120ms -> 320ms, p95 spiked. No errors in API gateway yet.
raj: grabbing logs, pulling kube events
lee: notifying customers? think it's internal warmup noise
sam: on it. checking autoscaler and recent deploys
incident-bot: Auto-silence policy not yet applied; subsequent pages will escalate
maria: logs: ```
2026-03-14T10:04:11Z runtime: kv-warmup start node=d-3-12
2026-03-14T10:04:12Z autoscaler: scaleUp to 2 pods
2026-03-14T10:04:13Z runtime: heavy gc on d-3-12
```
raj: looks like autoscaler flapped when a pod restarted; KV cache miss + short mem pressure
sam: mitigation attempt: draining node d-3-12 to prevent noisy warmup, `kubectl drain d-3-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
maria: confirming drain completed, replacing with prewarmed instance
pagerduty-bot: PD-1234 acknowledged by sam - incident status: acknowledged
lee: quick check on customer impact: no error-rate increase, small latency blips for a subset of long-seq models. ops dashboard shows <0.5% traffic affected
sam: putting an autoresolve in 2m if no repeat spikes. applying suppression rule for this signature for 5m to avoid churn
maria: adding follow-up: alert rule tweak ticket created - TICKET-4521
raj: handing to next oncall @lee for monitoring for 30m
lee: ack, watching dashboards, will escalate if it recurs
sam: thanks team :thumbsup: marking as resolved if stable
incident-bot: PD-1234 auto-resolved - reason: manual-silence + no new triggers
maria: postmortem note: root cause = autoscaler reacting to transient memory pressure during pod restart causing KV cache coldstarts. Next steps: adjust scale cooldown and prewarming policy.
lee: adding retrospective blurb to weekly ops note
sam: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
